pages.title: What a business website actually costs — and what drives the price
pages.description: Ask five agencies what a website costs and you will get five different answers, which is why the question feels impossible to answer. The price is not one number.

pages.title: The pages every business website needs
pages.description: Most business websites fail in the same quiet way: a visitor arrives, cannot find the answer they came for, and leaves. The fix is rarely a new design.

pages.title: You have Instagram. You still need a website.
pages.description: Instagram is a good place to be seen, and for many businesses it is where customers first find them. But a social profile is not a website, and treating it as one leaves your business exposed.

pages.title: How to choose a domain name for your business
pages.description: Your domain name is the address of your business online, and it is one of the few decisions about your website that is hard to change later.

pages.title: Website speed: a practical guide for business owners
pages.description: Website speed is one of those things nobody notices when it is good and everybody notices when it is bad.

pages.title: How Google finds and ranks your website
pages.description: Every day, people type questions into Google and click the first few results.

pages.title: Sitemaps and robots.txt, explained simply
pages.description: Two small files do a surprising amount of work behind the scenes of every website. A sitemap is a list of your pages, handed to search engines so they can find everything you have published.

pages.title: Image SEO: names, alt text, and compression
pages.description: Images do more than decorate a website. They show your work, explain your products, and make a page worth looking at.

pages.title: Local SEO: getting found in your city
pages.description: Most businesses serve a particular place. A plumber works in one city, a restaurant feeds one neighbourhood, a clinic treats patients from the surrounding area.

pages.title: How to write website copy that sells
pages.description: Most websites fail not because the business behind them is bad, but because the words on the page do not do their job.

pages.title: Turning social followers into website visitors
pages.description: A follower is not a customer until they take the next step.

pages.title: How to ask customers for reviews — without being awkward
pages.description: Most happy customers never leave a review, not because they are unhappy, but because nobody asked them, or because asking felt like too much effort.

pages.title: Contact forms that actually get replies
pages.description: A visitor who opens a contact form is already interested. They have found the business, decided it might be able to help, and are ready to start a conversation.

pages.title: The numbers a business should watch every week
pages.description: A business owner does not need to watch every number every day. A short weekly check of the right figures is enough to spot problems early, see what is working, and decide what to do next.

pages.title: AI for a business: practical uses that actually save time
pages.description: AI is talked about as if it can do everything for a business, and that is not true.

pages.title: Free developer tools that save an hour a week
pages.description: Most development work is not writing new code from scratch. It is reading messy data, checking a pattern, converting one format into another, and comparing two versions of the same file.

pages.title: Free security tools every business should know
pages.description: Security for a business is often a set of small habits done consistently, not a single large purchase.

pages.title: Free SEO and design tools for your website
pages.description: A website earns visitors when search engines can read it clearly and when people can read it comfortably.

pages.title: Free everyday tools: QR codes, PDFs, and the rest
pages.description: Not every useful tool is about writing code or ranking in search.

pages.title: Cold email that gets replies: the honest basics
pages.description: Cold email has a poor reputation, and much of it is deserved. Most cold emails are long, generic, and sent to people who never asked for them, so they are ignored or marked as spam.

pages.title: Why cold email lands in spam — and how to avoid it
pages.description: An email that lands in spam might as well not have been sent. The recipient never sees it, never replies, and never learns what you offered.

pages.title: Your business does not have a website yet. That is costing you customers every week.
pages.description: Most customers search first and visit second. If they cannot find you, they find someone else — not because you are worse, but because you are invisible.

pages.title: SEO basics: what Google actually needs from a business website
pages.description: SEO is not magic, and it is not a secret trick. It is making your site easy for Google to read, fast to load, and genuinely useful for the searcher.

pages.title: Why a fast site matters more than a fancy site
pages.description: A beautiful site that takes 8 seconds to load is a site most visitors never see. Speed is not a technical detail — it is the first impression.

pages.title: Social media for a business: steady beats viral
pages.description: You do not need a viral video. You need a customer to see you twice, trust you a little more, and remember you when they need you.

pages.title: Reviews are free market research — if you read them properly
pages.description: One star rating tells you almost nothing. Ten reviews, read together, tell you exactly what to fix next.

pages.title: Do you need a dashboard, or just a website? An honest answer
pages.description: Not every business needs a dashboard on day one. Some need a website and a phone that rings.

pages.title: What Kluzar does — and what it does not do
pages.description: Kluzar is a website agency and SaaS, serving businesses worldwide. It builds the website, hosts it, and manages it — so the business can run the business.
